messages:
jamie: Heads-up — I flipped a routing-weight config to send 5% traffic to v1.4.7-alpha for the canary. Question: do we treat this as a patch bump (1.4.7 -> 1.4.8) or a hotpatch (keep tag, add buildmeta)? Trying to be consistent for release notes and rollback expectations.

deploy-bot: @jamie deploy-bot noticed config change on service/api-surface by jamie. Suggested action: annotate release notes with [config-only]. No automated bump applied. :robot_face:

samir: My gut: config-only runtime routing changes that don't modify binaries shouldn't force a semver bump. We should avoid churn in tags for traffic-only ops.

anj: +1 but edge case: if the config change affects client-facing behavior (e.g., different model variant serving) then we should patch. How about rule: patch bump if user-visible change; otherwise just log and annotate.

elaine: We need a clear signal in release notes so SRE/CS can triage regressions. Proposal: add a small metadata tag in changelog entries like "[config-only][no-patch]" so release pages can filter.

lucy: Quick ops note — if we don't bump, rollbacks are dangerous because there won't be a new tag to point to for the undo. Can we rely on the config repo's deploy history instead?

jamie: Good point @lucy. For traffic routing changes we have atomic revert via the config repo. So rollback path exists without a new semver tag. That said, ops on customer-facing flags should probably get a patch bump.

samir: Also consider our deploybot heuristics: right now it auto-bumps on PRs with any changes under /pkg or /cmd. Config-only (under /configs) is ignored. Maybe we should codify that and add a check for whether the change touches protobufs or API contracts.

anj: We should also standardize buildmeta usage. Suggestion: reserve +hotpatch.buildmeta for emergency binary fixes that were cherry-picked to a stable tag. For config-only, use no buildmeta and no bump; append a changelog entry with `[cfg]`.

elaine: For release notes consumers (support dashboards), let's add a boolean field `is_semver_change` in our release metadata so their filters don't have to parse human text. deploy-bot could emit that.

deploy-bot: noted. Will propose a small PR to emit `is_semver_change: true|false` based on file paths and whether binaries changed. Drafting rule: files under /configs -> false; anything touching /api, /pkg, /models -> true.

jamie: TL;DR consensus: config-only routing change = no semver bump, annotate changelog with [config-only], rely on config-repo revert for rollbacks. Emergency binary hotfixes = patch bump + `+hotpatch` buildmeta if cherry-picked. I'll open a short RFC and a tiny deploy-bot PR to add `is_semver_change`. Thanks all :thumbsup:
